tagline: An eastern seaside province with Koh Samet, quiet beaches, fruit orchards, and famous dried seafood
introHtml:
Rayong sits east of Chonburi, about a 2–3 hour drive from Bangkok. It has the clear water of Koh Samet, the long and quiet Mae Ramphueng Beach, and orchards that ripen durian, rambutan, and mangosteen over the summer.

People like to drive down for the seafood, pick up shrimp paste and fish sauce to take home, then catch a boat out to Koh Samet to laze on the sand. If you want an easy trip, wander the Yom Chinda old town, try some noodles, stop at a cafe, and carry on to the coast at Ban Phe or the river mouth at Pak Nam Prasae.
bestTime: November–February, when the sea is clear and calm and good for island trips; April–June is orchard fruit season

highlights.name: Koh Samet
highlights.blurb: The island off Ban Phe, with clear water and white sand a short boat ride away. There's Sai Kaew Beach, Ao Phrao, and smaller coves to choose from for a stay

highlights.name: Mae Ramphueng Beach
highlights.blurb: A long sandy beach in Rayong town, with a beachfront road, seafood restaurants, and places to stay lined up along the water for a relaxed sit

highlights.name: Ban Phe
highlights.blurb: The pier for Koh Samet and the province's big souvenir market, selling shrimp paste, fish sauce, dried squid, and all sorts of dried seafood

highlights.name: Yom Chinda Road
highlights.blurb: An old town along the Rayong River, with old wooden buildings, nobles' houses, coffee shops, and local snacks to wander past

highlights.name: Pak Nam Prasae
highlights.blurb: An old fishing community at the mouth of the Prasae River, with HTMS Prasae moored as a memorial, the Prasae Sin Bridge, and the golden Prong mangrove field

highlights.name: Fruit orchards
highlights.blurb: Rayong is a durian, rambutan, and mangosteen town. In summer the orchards open up for all-you-can-eat fruit and to buy some to take home

foodScene.name: Beachfront seafood
foodScene.note: Mae Ramphueng Beach, Ban Phe, and the coast are lined with seafood spots serving fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, and squid at reasonable prices

foodScene.name: Dried seafood and shrimp paste & fish sauce
foodScene.note: Ban Phe sells dried squid, dried shrimp, shrimp paste, and Rayong's well-known fish sauce. People stop to buy them as gifts before heading back

foodScene.name: Rayong noodles and khanom chin
foodScene.note: In town there are long-running noodle shops and khanom chin with crab nam ya that locals have eaten for ages

foodScene.name: Durian, rambutan, mangosteen
foodScene.note: In summer Rayong's orchard fruit comes in fully. Mon Thong durian and Rong Rian rambutan are easy to find at stalls and orchards

foodScene.name: Sweets and local snacks
foodScene.note: Rayong has kalamae, khao lam, and folk sweets sold at the Ban Phe market and souvenir shops

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and by the sea
foodScene.note: The Yom Chinda area and Mae Ramphueng beachfront have cafes in old buildings and coffee shops with sea views to stop and rest

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and street food
foodScene.note: Around the residential areas and worker dorms near the industrial estate there are mu kratha (DIY hotpot-grill) spots and street food for an evening meal

attractions.name: Koh Samet
attractions.blurb: The clear-water island off Ban Phe, with Sai Kaew Beach, Ao Phrao, and small bays to swim and snorkel

attractions.name: Mae Ramphueng Beach
attractions.blurb: A long sandy beach in town, with a beachfront road, seafood restaurants, and seaside stays for watching the sunset

attractions.name: Yom Chinda Road
attractions.blurb: An old town along the Rayong River with antique wooden buildings, nobles' houses, cafes, and local food

attractions.name: Thung Prong Thong, Pak Nam Prasae
attractions.blurb: A mangrove forest with a wooden walkway out over green-gold Prong trees as far as the eye can see, at the Pak Nam Prasae community

attractions.name: HTMS Prasae
attractions.blurb: An old warship moored as a memorial at Pak Nam Prasae, which you can climb aboard to walk around and take in the river view

attractions.name: Sunthorn Phu Monument
attractions.blurb: A monument to the great poet in Klaeng district, his father's hometown, with statues of characters from Phra Aphai Mani to walk around

attractions.name: Khao Laem Ya–Mu Ko Samet National Park
attractions.blurb: A coastal and island area with viewpoints, quiet beaches, and nature trails from Mae Ramphueng Beach out to Koh Samet

attractions.name: Institute of Marine Science / Rayong Aquarium
attractions.blurb: An indoor spot to see fish and sea life, good for bringing kids and family along between beach trips
